status: IMPLEMENTED_CANDIDATE 0.2.14 / code 17; rising immersive sky implemented; 208 EditMode and 161 PlayMode passed; both APKs audited; physical-headset acceptance PENDING. Art redesign and removal of the optional creek pump are PROPOSAL ONLY.
user_intent: Reveal a surrounding sky/environment slowly from bottom to top on entering firefighting, then obscure the real surroundings; provide a scene beautification proposal and reconsider the second water device. Keep hand tracking.

implemented.scope: Standalone Emberdeep fireground only; scene-owned background, removed on leaving the scene.
implemented.timing: Approximately four eligible seconds after stable scene placement. Uses unscaled delta time with a 0.1-second per-frame cap. Focus, pause, head readiness and placement gate progression; recenter and sector advance do not reset it.
implemented.transition: Soft world-height mask reveals nadir to zenith. Initial framebuffer coverage is zero; final coverage is opaque. The transparent compositor underlay is progressively covered without switching off the passthrough provider.
implemented.art: Muted warm horizon and sun, cool upper sky, distant mountain ridge and two dark forest silhouette layers, with a dark lower hemisphere.
implemented.geometry: One inward-visible sphere follows camera position with fixed world rotation; no shadows, probes or active collider; URP shader with stereo instancing macros. It does not alter miniature scale or interaction positions.
implemented.lifecycle: Camera background is transparent while the sky owns it; the previous camera clear state is restored if still owned when destroyed. Material and geometry are scene-owned.
implemented.foreground: Fireground objects, UI and tracked hands retain their existing foreground rendering and input. No dwell selection, controller substitution or hand-tracking disable switch was introduced.

proposal_only.direction: Twilight forest rescue diorama; improve information hierarchy before adding asset complexity.
priorities: P1: Reduce persistent HUD and station signage. Make objective, remaining fires and water dominant; show detailed instructions contextually. Preserve target sizes and reachable hand interaction positions.

P2: Three muted foliage values, orange-red fire focus, grey-brown charred silhouettes and restrained wet-tree feedback. Integrate riverbanks and station foundations with soil, rocks and reeds while leaving hand paths clear.

P3: Vary repeating sky silhouettes, unify station materials and distinguish upgrades by structure. Keep peripheral scenery still and avoid new volumetric effects or extra real-time lights until measured on devices.

right_water_device.observed: The optional creek pump appears from sector two, requires intake placement and a pull/return stroke. Both manual pumps deliver 12 water per valid cycle; the primary upgrade path reaches 30 water/second. Left-hand mode mirrors station sides.
right_water_device.recommendation: Remove the second refill device from ordinary default layouts while retaining the creek scenery. Reserve the creek pump for a later main-supply-interruption mission with a distinct objective and reward; do not simply inflate its yield to compete with the primary station upgrade.
right_water_device.reason: Extra intake interaction currently adds neither a unique resource nor a distinct strategic benefit, while duplicating signage, hand targets and teaching burden.
right_water_device.implementation_status: PROPOSAL ONLY. Both stations, progression and refill values are unchanged in 0.2.14.

verification.new_coverage: Rendered alpha before/midway/after reveal; foreground visibility; no active collider; fixed world orientation; paused progress and bounded resume; camera state restoration; live-frame scene progression and camp cleanup.
verification.capture_scope: Live Editor frames, synthetic sector advancement, desktop camera. All four images visually reviewed. This is not a real headset or passthrough-compositor capture.
verification.device_acceptance: PENDING: actual compositor occlusion, stereo consistency, hand visibility, comfort and frame rate on PICO/Quest.
